subject: accountancy
question_text: State the meaning of a Trial Balance?
answer_text: Trial Balance is a statement prepared with debit and credit balances of all accounts in ledger, to verify the arithmetical accuracy of the accounts. It is prepared after balancing all the accounts of ledger. There are two columns in a Trial Balance: debit and credit. While debit side includes all the debit balances, credit side includes all the credit balances of the accounts. It also helps in preparing financial statements, as it is a summarise version of the ledger. It is generally prepared on monthly or yearly basis.
final_answer: Thus, a Trial Balance is essential for verifying the accuracy of accounts.
difficulty_reasoning: Direct recall of the definition of Trial Balance.

subject: accountancy
question_text: Give two examples of errors of commission?
answer_text: Errors of Commission refer to those errors that are committed when transactions are recorded with wrong amounts; wrong balancing or wrong posting and/or wrong carrying forwarding is done. Below given are the examples of error of commission: 1. Goods purchased worth Rs 20,000 on credit are recorded in the Purchases Book as Rs 10,000. This transaction should have been recorded in the Purchases Book with an amount of Rs 20,000; however, it was recorded as Rs 10,000. This is an error due to wrong recording of amount. 2. Total of Sales Book is carried forward as Rs 5,000 instead of Rs 500. In this case, wrong amount is carried forwarded from one accounting period to another or from an end of one page to the beginning of another page. This is referred to as an error of carrying forward.
final_answer: Thus, these examples highlight how errors of commission can lead to inaccuracies in financial records.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of different types of accounting errors.

subject: accountancy
question_text: What are the different types of errors that are usually committed in recording business transaction?

question_image.description: Mathematical representation related to errors in accounting.

answer_text: 1. Errors of omission- When an entry gets omitted during recording in the book of original entry or during posting the transaction, then error of omission is committed. There are two types of errors of omission, viz.: Partial omission and Complete omission. 2. Errors of principle- These refer to those errors that are committed when recording of transactions in the book of the original entry is done against the accounting principle. 3. Errors of commission- These refer to those errors that are committed when transactions are recorded with wrong amounts, wrong balancing, wrong posting and/or wrong carrying forwarded is done. 4. Compensating errors- When effects of one error are cancelled by the effects of another error of an equal amount, then compensating errors are committed.
final_answer: Thus, various types of errors include errors of omission, principle, commission, and compensating errors.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of different types of accounting errors.
